description.short_caption: Erythematous papules and plaques with crusting on the lower back.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the lower back of a patient with numerous erythematous papules and plaques, some of which have central crusting. The lesions are scattered and vary in size, with no clear pattern of distribution. The surrounding skin appears otherwise normal. The findings are suggestive of a dermatologic or infectious process.

description.short_caption: Multiple hyperpigmented macules and papules on the lower back and buttocks.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the lower back and buttocks of a patient with numerous hyperpigmented macules and papules. The lesions are scattered and vary in size, with some appearing slightly raised. The distribution is diffuse, and the lesions do not appear to be clustered. The skin surrounding the lesions appears otherwise normal without significant erythema or scaling.
visible_findings: diffuse distribution on lower back and buttocks

description.short_caption: PAS stain of skin biopsy showing fungal elements in the stratum corneum.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin stained with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS). The epidermis and stratum corneum are visible, with fungal elements highlighted in magenta within the stratum corneum. The dermis appears unremarkable. The PAS stain is used to identify polysaccharides in fungal cell walls, making fungal elements stand out distinctly.
visible_findings: fungal elements stained magenta in the stratum corneum

description.short_caption: GMS stain of a skin biopsy showing fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a GMS (Gomori methenamine silver) stain of a skin biopsy. The epidermis and underlying dermis are visible, with fungal elements stained black against a green background. The fungal structures appear elongated and filamentous, consistent with hyphae. The stain highlights the fungal organisms, aiding in their identification within the tissue.
visible_findings: green background typical of GMS stain
skin layers visible, including epidermis and dermis
